author: jd3n2309
quote:
The game was overhyped. It has achieved one feat and it's showing us how strong consumerism can be. Nominating a game for game of the year without even seeing gameplay of it is crazy. 

Now if this were only hype created by the fans, it wouldn't have been so bad, but rockstar paid the media to overhype the game. It has got to the point where even if the game was industry-breaking, and perfect, it would still fall short from people's unrealistic expectations. 

The gameplay just straight up ****. It feels like a GTA 5 DLC. The characters are bland and you can tell rockstar put effort into not offending anyone to retain as much of a market as possible. This is profoundly "un-GTA". 

It seems like Rockstar have taken it upon themselves to play parents to society through their game, thinking they can offer gamers "life lessons" through having to have an appease your NPC girlfriend.

The story is boring, the main charactere bland, the game sacrifices realism for fun. But is still completely unrealistic in other areas. Flipping a car back on its wheels for example. 

I don't think it's terrible, it's just kind of mediocre. Which is highly disappointed after so much paid advertisement and hype. 

Essentially, the game feels like GTA 5.1 because they ran out of DLC content to sell people in GTA 5. The campaign just feels like a vessel for the to-be heavily commercialized GTA 6 online. 

Anyone leaving a 99 or 100 is either still wearing the rose tinted glasses created by all the hype, or are paid/incentivised reviwers. It's unfortunate rockstar are incentivising reviewers to leave them perfect scores because they clearly need the feedback. Your game is not perfect. If you had true confidence in your game, you would not need the disingenuous marketing. 

13 years to release a lagging 30fps relationship simulator that still has bugs on release.
